                    ### Question
                    A 64-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after the onset of right-sided weakness and impaired speech. On admission, she is diagnosed with thrombotic stroke and treatment with alteplase is begun. Neurologic examination four weeks later shows residual right hemiparesis. A CT scan of the head shows hypoattenuation in the territory of the left middle cerebral artery. Which of the following processes best explains this finding?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Gangrenous necrosis
opb. Coagulative necrosis
opc. Liquefactive necrosis
opd. Caseous necrosis
ope. Fat necrosis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The finding of hypoattenuation in the territory of the left middle cerebral artery in the CT scan of the head is best explained by coagulative necrosis. This is due to the ischemia in the affected brain tissue leading to hypoxia and nutrient deprivation, resulting in cell death characteristic of coagulative necrosis. The evidence paths support the relationship between oxygen deprivation, ischemia, and coagulative necrosis.
